clue.text: Stage laugh, reverse of demure, greeting start of knockabout

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its last letter back to its first
the start of a word is just its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: coy means modest or demure
first letter of knockabout

explanation.surface: A stage direction for a laugh that greets a coy performer at the start of a slapstick turn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greeting' simply has the reversed word meet the single letter that follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: Yock is theatrical slang for a loud belly laugh from an audience, a variant of yuk.

clue.text: An ugly totty on street gave old-fashioned leer

definitions.note: past tense, matching the Spenserian past tense of glance

indicators.note: totty is a Scots word for dizzy or unsteady, so the letters beside it stagger out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
ST is the usual abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: An unattractive tipsy woman out on the street ogled passers-by in an antique way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Totty' looks like slang for an attractive woman, but here it is the Scots adjective meaning dizzy, and it shakes up the letters. ST is attached to the fodder by 'on'.
explanation.definitionFit: Yglaunst is Spenser's archaic past tense of glance, so it means cast a sidelong look or leer.

clue.text: Army chief hosts regiment hooley?

explanation.definitionFit: Craic is Irish for fun and lively conversation, the very thing a hooley, a rowdy Irish get-together, provides.

clue.text: Ron Kray, not the first banged up in part of cell

explanation.definitionFit: Karyon is a term for the nucleus, the central structure inside a living cell.

clue.text: Disquiet with nomad registering measure of certain rays

a Rom is a Romani person, traditionally a traveller

explanation.surface: A worried wanderer registers on some instrument that measures radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: The angstrom is a tiny unit of length used to state the wavelengths of light and X-rays.

clue.text: Stock-jobbing, contagious in part

clue.text: Old disturbed with ire, annoyed

clue.text: Company got up to dance, lyric, with four pairs of feet

clue.text: Complaint from fellow with nothing inside

clue.text: What for him is oily is shoved into gearbox slots

definitions.text: What for him is oily is shoved into gearbox slots

indicators.note: shoving something into another thing puts it inside, so the earlier pieces go within

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the answer: the 'him' is a garage hand, and an oily rag is the mark of one. A gearbox gate is the guide plate with slots for each gear.
explanation.definitionFit: A garagiste is a person who runs or works in a garage, the sort of man always holding an oily rag.

clue.text: Board of a sort at fringes of Chester ground? The Durham one, anyway (11, two words)

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a sightscreen is the large white board at the boundary that helps the batsman see the ball.

clue.text: Grass field lass goes round, bordering river

clue.text: The old take horse from trough in riding to 'ounds
